'''Winfred O'Neal Tubbs''' (born September 24, 1970) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player. A 6'4", {{convert|254|lb|abbr=on}}. [[linebacker]] from the [[University of Texas at Austin|University of Texas]], Tubbs was selected by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the third round of the [[1994 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1994 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1994/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played seven [[National Football League]] (NFL) seasons from 1994 to 2000 for the Saints and [[San Francisco 49ers]]. He was selected to the Pro Bowl in 1998, and was named All-NFL (second team) in 1997.

Winfred Tubbs is perhaps best known for his appearance in the arcade football game [[NFL Blitz]].

Tubbs, now an [[entrepreneur]], writes a blog on finance and investing for [[MSN Money|MSN Money's]] "The Invested Life."<ref>{{cite web | url = http://theinvestedlife.msnbc.msn.com/investor.aspx?type=blog&aid=i_1&id=26293332&source=msn&gt1=25074#/bio/i_1// | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20101212155624/http://theinvestedlife.msnbc.msn.com/investor.aspx?type=blog&aid=i_1&id=26293332&source=msn&GT1=25074#/bio/i_1// | url-status = dead | archive-date = 2010-12-12 | title = Winfred Tubbs Bio - The Invested Life | publisher = MSN | accessdate = 2011-01-26 }}</ref>

'''Woodrow Lowe''' (June 9, 1954 – November 6, 2025) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a  [[linebacker]] for the [[San Diego Chargers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1976 to 1986. Lowe played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]] under head coach [[Bear Bryant]] from 1972 to 1975. A three-time, first-team [[All-America college football team|All-American]], Lowe earned consensus honors in 1974 and was inducted into the [[College Football Hall of Fame]]. He was named to the [[San Diego Chargers 40th Anniversary Team|Chargers' 40th]] and [[San Diego Chargers 50th Anniversary Team|50th anniversary teams]]. After retiring from playing, Lowe coached at the high school, college, and professional levels.

'''Wylie Dewayen Turner''' (born April 19, 1957) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Turner was born on April 19, 1957, in [[Dallas, Texas]], where he attended [[W. T. White High School]].<ref name="PFR">{{cite web | url = https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TurnWy20.htm | title = Wylie Turner Stats | website = Pro-Football-Reference.com | access-date = March 19, 2024 | archive-date = October 30, 2023 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20231030120156/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TurnWy20.htm | url-status = live }}</ref> In high school, he played football and ran track-and-field. Although he signed a letter of intent with [[Texas Southern University]], he ended up going to [[Angelo State University]] so that he could run track-and-field and play for their [[Angelo State Rams football|football team]]. He started out as a running back, but was converted to cornerback.<ref>{{Cite news | url = https://www.newspapers.com/article/abilene-reporter-news-turner-among-naia/143705231/ | title = Turner among NAIA sprint specialists | last = Hart | first = Bill | date = May 10, 1978 | access-date = March 19, 2024 | newspaper = [[Abilene Reporter-News]] | type = clipping | via = [[Newspapers.com]] | page = C1 | archive-date = March 19, 2024 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20240319222455/https://www.newspapers.com/article/abilene-reporter-news-turner-among-naia/143705231/ | url-status = live }}</ref> He was also the team's kick returner, leading college football in return yard average in 1977, which included a 104-yard return for a touchdown.<ref name="DASH"/> Turner became an accomplished college track-and-field runner, competing in the [[100 metres|100-meter]] and [[200 metres|200-meter]] dashes.<ref>{{Cite news | url = https://www.newspapers.com/article/san-angelo-standard-times-turner-redemp/143705200/ | title = Turner, Redemption Set Date | last = Rudnicki | first = Frank | date = April 11, 1978 | access-date = March 19, 2024 | newspaper = [[San Angelo Standard-Times]] | type = clipping | via = [[Newspapers.com]] | page = 8A | archive-date = March 19, 2024 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20240319222456/https://www.newspapers.com/article/san-angelo-standard-times-turner-redemp/143705200/ | url-status = live }}</ref> He was the [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] champion at 200-meters in 1977.<ref name="DASH"/>

Turner went undrafted in the [[1979 NFL draft]].<ref name="PFR"/> He signed as a free agent with the [[Denver Broncos]] but was cut from the team in August 1979.<ref>{{Cite news | url = https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daily-sentinel-broncos-release-a-no/143705998/ | title = Broncos release a No. 1; 'Gorillas' lose Gerela | agency = [[Associated Press]] | date = August 22, 1979 | access-date = March 19, 2024 | newspaper =  | type = clipping | via = [[Newspapers.com]] | page = 21 | archive-date = March 19, 2024 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20240319222456/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daily-sentinel-broncos-release-a-no/143705998/ | url-status = live }}</ref> He then signed with the [[Green Bay Packers]] the next month. During the [[1979 NFL season]], he was primarily a back-up and [[special teams]] player, recording 12 total tackles and recovering one onside kick.<ref name="DASH">{{Cite news | url = https://www.newspapers.com/article/green-bay-press-gazette-wylie-turner/143704984/ | title = Wylie Turner | date = September 7, 1980 | access-date = March 19, 2024 | newspaper = [[Green Bay Press-Gazette]] | type = clipping | via = [[Newspapers.com]] | page = 24 | archive-date = March 19, 2024 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20240319222456/https://www.newspapers.com/article/green-bay-press-gazette-wylie-turner/143704984/ | url-status = live }}</ref> Turner played for the Packers for a total of two seasons, appearing in 28 games and recording 2 interceptions.<ref name="PFR"/> He was competing for the starting cornerback position prior to the [[1981 NFL season]] but did not play for the Packers that year.<ref>{{Cite news | url = https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-oshkosh-northwestern-packers-second/143704936/ | title = Packers' secondary feels heat of competition | last = Woodrow | first = Tom | date = August 1, 1981 | access-date = March 19, 2024 | newspaper = [[The Oshkosh Northwestern]] | type = clipping | via = [[Newspapers.com]] | page = B2 | archive-date = March 19, 2024 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20240319222457/https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-oshkosh-northwestern-packers-second/143704936/ | url-status = live }}</ref><ref name="PFR"/>

Turner later played in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) for the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] from 1982 to 1986 and the [[Ottawa Rough Riders]] in 1986.<ref name="pfa"/> He was named a [[CFL West]] All-Star in 1985.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.statscrew.com/football/stats/p-turnewyl001 | title=Wylie Turner | publisher=Stats Crew | accessdate=6 August 2025}}</ref>

Turner was inducted into the Angelo State Sports Hall of Honor in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://angelosports.com/honors/hall-of-honor/wylie-turner/39 | title = Wylie Turner | access-date = March 19, 2024 | website = AngeloSports.com | archive-date = June 27, 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200627143018/https://angelosports.com/honors/hall-of-honor/wylie-turner/39 | url-status = live }}</ref>
